observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2) creates a new array using the component type of array1. When array2 contains elements incompatible with array1's component type, System.arraycopy throws an ArrayStoreException. The implementation lacks a validation check to ensure type compatibility before performing the copy.
hypothesis: The method ArrayUtils.addAll creates a new array based on the component type of the first array (array1). When array2 contains elements that are not assignable to the component type of array1, System.arraycopy throws an ArrayStoreException. The method lacks a validation check to ensure that all elements in array2 are compatible with the component type of the resulting array before attempting the copy.
prediction: The implementation will lack a check for type compatibility between the elements of array2 and the component type of array1.
experiment_rationale: The provided code snippet clearly shows the creation of the array using type1 (from array1) and the subsequent direct call to System.arraycopy without any validation of the contents of array2 against type1.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a missing validation check. The code assumes that array2 can be copied into an array of type1's component type. When this assumption is violated, the system throws an ArrayStoreException. Adding a check to validate the compatibility of array2's elements with the target array type would prevent this and allow for a more descriptive exception (like IllegalArgumentException) as requested in the bug report.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not the algorithm itself, but the lack of a guard/check to ensure the input data is valid for the chosen algorithm.
The method signature is correct; the issue is internal validation of the provided arguments.
